_header: ===== cherrypick-pmcc — PMCC deep-ITM covered calls on XSP, QQQ, GLD, IWM and SLV (paper-only) =====
_what_this_is: A deep-ITM call with a short call sold against it, three ways (the arms block). control: buy an 85-90-delta call at ~21 DTE, sell the ATM call nearest spot at ~7 DTE, hold to the short's expiration and close both. shield and shield_hold (2026-10-05): Tom King's 'Income Shield' -- hold a ~1-year 0.90-0.95-delta call and roll a 0.70-delta weekly short against it until the long reaches 45 DTE. tv_close_threshold/tv_managed_exit remain an advisor-tunable exit experiment on control's advised twins. Early assignment on the physical symbols is REFUSED-around (the dividends block) and MEASURED, never modelled; XSP carries neither risk (see _settlement_style_note). Copy to config.json (git-ignored) or ~/.cherrypick/config/pmcc.json.
_symbols_note: XSP (Mini-SPX, European, cash-settled), QQQ, GLD, IWM and SLV (American, physical delivery) since the 2026-10-05 shield boundary (docs/shield-study.md has why each and why not the rest); TQQQ before it, and still declared in occ_roots, settlement_style and dividends so its open positions settle -- remove it once none is open. Every arm trades every symbol, one position per (symbol, arm) at a time; max_positions bounds each arm's concurrent positions summed across symbols. A symbol not declared in settlement_style is refused at entry (unknown_settlement). Symbols are never pooled: each is its own population.
_occ_roots_note: The OCC root the provider admits per underlying. Leveraged ETFs split often, and a split leaves ADJUSTED roots (TQQQ1) sharing expiration dates with the standard root; only the configured root is priced, and an expiration listing only adjusted roots refuses `not_root_listed`. After a split, verify the standard root re-lists before resuming — and treat a split mid-position as a manual `--settle` plus a measurement break (unmodelled). XSP does not split, so its root is simply itself.
_settlement_style_note: How each symbol's expiring legs settle. TQQQ is `physical` — American delivery: an ITM short call hands over 100 short shares per contract at the settlement print, covered the NEXT session together with the long's sale (the combined disposal), so a Friday assignment carries short shares over the weekend. Delivered shares are booked at the SETTLEMENT SPOT, not the strike — the calendars decomposition, which keeps physical settlement exactly cash-plus-a-share-leg. XSP is `cash` — European exercise style, so it can ONLY be exercised at its own expiration: there is no early-assignment risk to refuse around (the dividends block below has no XSP entry and none is needed — `_entry_guards` in paper_loop.py only runs the ex-dividend check for `physical` symbols) and no delivered-share path ever fires for it (`assignment_from` is only called from the `physical` branch of `book.settle_expiring_legs`). `management.assignment_exposed` is likewise exempt for `cash` positions — see its docstring. A symbol declared as neither style is refused at entry.
_dividends_note: PHYSICAL-settlement symbols only. A short whose life [sale day, expiration] spans a declared ex-dividend date is REFUSED (ex_dividend_span): an ITM short call is really assigned at the close before the ex-date, and this module deliberately does not model early assignment. At entry the whole entry is refused; on a held-long position the roll is, and the position runs without a short until a later day clears the date (the tracker counts those weeks). Skipped outright for `cash`-settled XSP. Dates are DECLARED from the issuer's own schedule and never computed or fetched; a non-paying trust (GLD, SLV) is declared with an empty list. REFRESH BEFORE declared_through: a span past it refuses entry (dividend_calendar_lapsed) rather than assuming itself dividend-free, so a lapsed table stops entries loudly, by design.

TQQQ._source: ProShares own distribution schedule (proshares.com/resources/distributions/distribution-schedule), verified 2026-08-24: Q3 ex 9/23 payable 9/29, Q4 ex 12/23 payable 12/30, plus the POTENTIAL excise-tax distribution ex 12/31 payable 1/7/2027 (included deliberately -- refusing a week that might carry an ex-date is the safe direction). Cross-checked against an independent aggregator, which agreed on 9/23; this module's docs record that aggregators disagree by a day, so the issuer page is the authority and a second source is the check on it. DECLARED, never fetched -- nothing on a loop path may touch the network. Refresh by hand from the issuer page before an entry can span past declared_through; a lapse stops entries loudly, by design.

QQQ._source: Invesco publishes no forward US distribution schedule we could find (checked 2026-10-04). The issuer's own Q3 2026 notice puts the record date on the Monday after the quarter's third Friday (2026-09-21), which under T+1 settlement is the US ex-date, and the 2026 ex-dates on file follow it (03-23, 06-22, 09-21). Q4 2026 = 2026-12-21, as two aggregators also state (marketchameleon, stockanalysis). DECLARED, never fetched. Refresh by mid-December with the Q1 2027 date (expected 2027-03-22): a span past declared_through refuses entry (dividend_calendar_lapsed), loudly, by design.

IWM._source: iShares' own 2026-2028 Fund Distributions Schedule (ishares.com, as of 2026-09-30; IWM is in the quarterly equity group: ex 3 business days before the third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec), verified 2026-10-04. The 2026 dates already past (03-17, 06-15, 09-15) match the dividend history on file. Includes BlackRock's POTENTIAL late-December excise distribution (2026-12-30, 2027-12-30) deliberately -- refusing a week that might carry an ex-date is the safe direction. DECLARED, never fetched.

GLD._source: A grantor trust holding gold bullion: it pays no distributions (none in the dividend history on file since 2011, nor in tastytrade's). Declared empty rather than left out, so the physical-settlement check reads an answer instead of a lapse. Re-check if the trust changes.

SLV._source: A grantor trust holding silver bullion: it pays no distributions (none in the dividend history on file since 2011, nor in tastytrade's). Declared empty rather than left out, so the physical-settlement check reads an answer instead of a lapse. Re-check if the trust changes.

_source_note: stream_cache_db overrides the shared stream cache path; null means the suite default (~/.cherrypick/data/marketdata/stream_cache.db). This module is a pure READ-ONLY consumer of that cache — its two expirations are served by the streamer's `expirations` request field, and its deep strikes by the `window_hints` field, both declared automatically every tick.
_dte_note: The short lands on the soonest Friday with DTE in [short_dte_min, short_dte_max] (~7 days); the long on the Friday in [long_dte_min, long_dte_max] nearest long_dte_target (~21 days). The short window is deliberately at least as wide as the 7-day weekly spacing (5-11) so every weekday finds a qualifying Friday — narrower windows leave gaps on some weekdays. Computed from the calendar, asserted against the cache — never nearest-matched from the chain.
_selection_note: 2026-08-23 redesign. LONG: long_delta_min/long_delta_max define a DELTA BAND (default 0.85-0.90, not a floor) — the candidate whose delta falls in the band, nearest the band's midpoint, wins; a tie prefers the higher strike. With no greeks on file the candidate falls back to the pre-redesign heuristic (highest strike whose extrinsic is at most max_long_extrinsic per share) and the row records long_selected_by='extrinsic' so degraded entries stay excludable; a KNOWN delta outside the band is simply excluded, never laundered through the fallback. allow_extrinsic_fallback (default true) gates that degrade — set false to require a real delta on every candidate. SHORT: no yield floor and no ITM-only restriction any more — the short is the strike NEAREST spot, whichever side it lands on (ties prefer the ITM side). This can leave the short OTM; the worksheet math floors short_intrinsic at 0 in that case.
_management_note: The default control exit HOLDS the position to the short's own expiration and then closes both legs together (`short_expiration`) — no more early tv-exhaustion trigger, no more roll book, no more breach special case (the short can legitimately sit OTM by construction). tv_close_threshold and the new tv_managed_exit boolean remain as a live, advisor-tunable escape hatch back to the pre-redesign early-exit behavior: set only through an advised:control row's frozen advice_params overlay, never through this file, so the suite can run hold-to-expiry vs. early-tv-exit as a paper A/B. assignment_exposure_tv: marks with short extrinsic under this are flagged assignment-exposed — pure telemetry bounding what unmodelled early assignment could have touched. disposition_time is when delivered shares are covered and orphan longs sold the session after a settlement. exec_window_start gates ALL management action until the open stabilizes; max_leg_spread_pct is the is-this-mark-actionable bar (deep-ITM spreads are the module's known risk #2 — the attempts table measures how often this refuses).
_window_note: deep_window_pct bounds the entry snapshot's quote fetch: strikes in [spot*(1-deep_window_pct), spot*1.02]. The 85-90-delta long (2026-08-23 redesign) sits much closer to spot than the old ~99-delta design, so this dropped from 0.45 to 0.20 — via stream_window's window_hints, this is what makes the module's long-leg quotes exist at all.

defaults._deep_window_by_symbol_note: Per-symbol override for deep_window_pct, because one shared bound is necessarily sized for the DEEPEST symbol and buys every other one strikes it cannot use. Measured 2026-08-24 against the live chain: an 85-90-delta call at ~21 DTE sat 15.2-18.8% ITM on TQQQ (strikes 56.0-58.5 against a 68.995 spot) but only 4.0% ITM on XSP (734 against 764.5) -- a 3x leveraged ETF carries several times a broad index's implied volatility. A single 0.20 therefore gives TQQQ a correct window and XSP roughly five times the strikes it can use, which is what made XSP the largest window in the suite. Unset symbols fall back to deep_window_pct, so this is additive. Re-derive per symbol rather than inheriting these numbers -- see docs/window-parameters.md.
defaults._max_leg_spread_pct_note: max_leg_spread_pct is enforced on BOTH paths since 2026-08-28: engine.plan_entry refuses an entry whose long or short leg quotes wider than this (spread_too_wide), and management.execution_gate still blocks acting on a mark that does. Until that date it was the exit path only, so nothing measured the spread being PAID at entry -- curve and bwb both hold this parameter at the same default and check it at entry, and pmcc was the outlier. Measured over all 8 entries before the change: seven at 0.018-0.072 (deep-ITM long legs included) and one at 0.293. Recalibrating this is a config change plus a journaled break, per the module's own honesty rules.
defaults._account_policy_note: Read only by held-long arms (control ignores it), so paper shield trades under its live twin's account rules. ira: every expiring short is bought back before the bell at any moneyness, since an IRA cannot carry short stock. margin: a short further than pin_buffer_pct out of the money may expire.

_books_note: Three arms from the 2026-10-05 shield boundary. `control` (since 2026-08-23): a 21-DTE long re-bought every cycle, an ATM weekly short, both closed at the short's expiry. `shield` and `shield_hold`: Tom King's held-long design, a ~1-year long held while a weekly 0.70-delta short rolls against it; they share one entry plan and differ only in that shield also rolls early (85% of the short's extrinsic decayed, or spot at its strike) and shield_hold holds each short to Friday. An arm other than control that this block does not declare stays off. The `advised:<experiment>` twins shadow control only.

shield._note: Held-long arm (2026-10-05 boundary, docs/shield-study.md). What makes it itself is in code, engine.ARM_RULES, so this block tunes it but cannot turn it into a copy of control: a ~1-year long (the third-Friday monthly nearest 360 DTE in [240, 540]) chosen by delta in [0.90, 0.95], no extrinsic fallback; a 0.70-delta weekly short (band 0.65-0.78, soonest Friday 5-11 DTE, above the long's strike), rolled on its expiry day from the close - 60m with a buyback-only deadline at close - 20m; closed when the long reaches 45 DTE or P&L to date reaches -30% of the long's cost, re-entering the next session. entry_symbols_per_session staggers first entries across the five symbols during the rollout. deep_window_pct_by_symbol here is this arm's own: its long sits 20-40% in the money where control's sits 4-10%.

shield_hold._note: Held-long arm (2026-10-05 boundary, docs/shield-study.md). What makes it itself is in code, engine.ARM_RULES, so this block tunes it but cannot turn it into a copy of control: a ~1-year long (the third-Friday monthly nearest 360 DTE in [240, 540]) chosen by delta in [0.90, 0.95], no extrinsic fallback; a 0.70-delta weekly short (band 0.65-0.78, soonest Friday 5-11 DTE, above the long's strike), rolled on its expiry day from the close - 60m with a buyback-only deadline at close - 20m; closed when the long reaches 45 DTE or P&L to date reaches -30% of the long's cost, re-entering the next session. entry_symbols_per_session staggers first entries across the five symbols during the rollout. deep_window_pct_by_symbol here is this arm's own: its long sits 20-40% in the money where control's sits 4-10%.

_stream_window_note: How wide an ATM window this module asks the producer for (window_hints). base_width is the ESCALATION FLOOR only -- it is NOT a suppression threshold and NOT a mirror of the producer's default, both of which it was until 2026-08-27. It claimed to mirror `window_strike_count`, and stopped being true when that was cut 60 -> 30 in the 2026-08-24 subscription incident: any computed need between 31 and 60 was then silently swallowed here while the producer served 30. TQQQ's structural need is 39 and sat squarely in that dead band. The hint is now emitted whatever it computes and the producer resolves max(default, hint) at the other end, so there is no duplicated constant left to drift. increment/decay_after_minutes stay at this deployment's tuned values (60/1440) rather than the module's 30/60 defaults -- widened after the 2026-08-17 incident where a faster-decaying escalation recycled the streamer every ~5 minutes for two hours. The union across modules takes the max per symbol, so this can never narrow anyone else.
_tastytrade_costs_note: Overrides for the shared cost model (cherrypick.core.fees.DEFAULT_COSTS): slippage_frac_of_spread, slippage_cap_frac_of_mid, commissions. Empty means the suite defaults. The per-symbol pieces are automatic and this is the one place TQQQ and XSP genuinely differ in the fee stack: TQQQ is an ETF and is off the broad-based index exchange-fee schedule entirely, while XSP IS a broad-based index option and is looked up on cherrypick.core.fees.INDEX_EXCHANGE_FEE_PER_CONTRACT by symbol (currently $0.00/contract under 10 contracts/leg — the same number as the ETF default today, but wired through the index schedule rather than an ETF exemption, so a future rate change there reaches XSP automatically). Every ITM expiry costs the $5 settlement/assignment event regardless of symbol; only TQQQ's physical assignments add the SEC/FINRA pass-throughs on the share side (XSP never reaches that path).
advice_header: ===== the advised book (paper only, off by default) =====
_advice_note: When enabled AND the suite's advisor covers this module (advisor.modules.pmcc in the orchestrator config — both switches must agree), the session's admitted advice opens one `advised:<experiment name>` book PER concurrent advisor experiment beside control (since 2026-09-17; a single `advised:control` before), each with its own admitted params FROZEN on each row at entry and restated through management.effective_params at every later tick. base_book must be 'control' — it is the only book left. The one thing worth advising right now is the hold-to-expiry vs. early-tv-exit experiment: tv_managed_exit flips the exit rule, tv_close_threshold tunes the early-exit trigger when it does.
live_header: ===== live gate (placeholder — see the module CLAUDE.md's Live-trading prerequisites) =====
_live_note: This module has NO live loop, no order-placement code, and no live account designation. `enabled` exists only so the suite's config/console surfaces can read a real gate for this module instead of reporting an absent one as 'unknown' — flipping it to true does nothing until a live loop is built, and post-assignment management plus a calculated ex-div decision (the module CLAUDE.md's prerequisites) land first. Guarded the same as every other live gate: hand-edit only, never through the settings surface.
